translations.text: The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
Abraham was the father of Isaac, Isaac the father of Jacob, and Jacob the father of Judah and his brothers.
Judah was the father of Perez and Zerah by Tamar. Perez was the father of Ephrom, and Ephrom the father of Aram.
Aram was the father of Amminadab, Amminadab the father of Nahshon, and Nahshon the father of
Boaz by Rahab. Boaz was the father of Obed by Ruth, and Obed the father of Jesse.
Jesse was the father of King David. King David was the father of Solomon by Uriah’s wife.
Solomon was the father of Rehoboam, Rehoboam the father of Abijah, and Abijah the father of Asa.
Asa was the father of Jehoshaphat, Jehoshaphat the father of Joram, and Joram the father of Uzziah.
Uzziah was the father of Jotham, Jotham the father of Ahaz, and Ahaz the father of Hezekiah.
Hezekiah was the father of Manasseh, Manasseh the father of Amos, and Amos the father of Josiah.
Josiah was the father of Jeconiah and his brothers at the time of the deportation to Babylon.
After the deportation to Babylon, Jeconiah was the father of Shealtiel, and Shealtiel the father of Zerubbabel.
Zerubbabel was the father of Abiud, Abiud the father of Eliakim, and Eliakim the father of Azor.
Azor was the father of Zadok, Zadok the father of Achim, and Achim the father of Eliud.
Eliud was the father of Eleazar, Eleazar the father of Matthan, and Matthan the father of Jacob.
Jacob was the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, from whom Jesus was born, who is called Christ.

So all the generations from Abraham to David were fourteen generations; from David to the deportation to Babylon, fourteen generations; and from the deportation to Babylon to Christ, fourteen generations.
Now the birth of Christ took place in this way. When his mother Mary was betrothed to Joseph, before they came together, she was found to be pregnant by the Holy Spirit.
Joseph her husband, being a righteous man and not wanting to expose her publicly, decided to divorce her secretly.

While he was considering this, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, “Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife, for what is conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.
She will give birth to a son, and you will name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.”
All this happened so that what the Lord had spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled:
“Look, the virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and she will name him Emmanuel,” which means “God is with us.”
When Joseph woke from sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him and took his wife.
He did not have sexual relations with her until she had given birth to her firstborn son, and he named him Jesus.
When Jesus was born in Bethlehem in Judea, in the days of King Herod, wise men from the east came to Jerusalem, saying,
“Where is the newborn king of the Jews? For we saw his star in the east and have come to worship him.”
When King Herod heard this, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
He gathered all the chief priests and the scribes of the people and asked them where the Christ was to be born.
They said to him, “In Bethlehem in Judea, for this is what was written by the prophet:
‘And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah, for from you will come a ruler who will shepherd my people Israel.’”
Then Herod [?] summoned the wise men and learned from them the time when the star had appeared.
He sent them to Bethlehem and said, “Go and inquire carefully about the child. When you find him, tell me, so that I too may go and worship him.”
After listening to the king, they went to the east. [?] went before them until it came and stood above the place where the child was.
When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceedingly great joy.
They entered the house and saw the child with Mary his mother. They fell down and worshiped him. Then they opened their treasures and offered him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
Having received an answer in a dream, they did not return to Herod but went back to their own country by another route.

When the wise men had departed, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream, saying, “Get up, take the child and his mother, and flee to Egypt. Stay there until I tell you, for Herod intends to search for the child to destroy him.”
He got up, took the child and his mother by night, and departed for Egypt.
He stayed there until Herod’s death, so that what the Lord had spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled: “Out of Egypt I called my son.”

Then Herod, seeing that the wise men had deceived him, became very angry. He sent men and killed all the boys in Bethlehem and throughout its surrounding territory who were two years old and younger, according to the time he had learned from the wise men.
Then what had been spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled:
“A voice was heard in Ramah, weeping, lamentation, and loud wailing: Rachel weeping for her children. She would not be comforted, because they were no more.”
When Herod died, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream in Egypt,
saying, “Get up, take the child and his mother, and go to the land of Israel, for those who sought the child’s life have died.”
He got up, took the child and his mother, and entered the land of Israel.
But when he heard that Archelaus was ruling in Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there. Having received a warning in a dream, he withdrew to the region of Galilee.
He came and settled in a town called Nazareth, so that what had been spoken through the prophets might be fulfilled: “He will be called a Nazarene.”
At that time, John the Baptist came, preaching in the wilderness [?],
saying, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has drawn near.”
For this is the one spoken of by the prophet Isaiah, who said, “The voice of one crying out in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight.”
John himself wore a garment of camel’s hair and a leather belt around his waist. His food was locusts and wild honey.
Then Jerusalem, all Judea, and the whole Judean region went out to him.
And they were baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.
At that time Jesus came from Galilee to John at the Jordan to be baptized by him.
But John tried to prevent him, saying, “I want to be baptized by you, yet you come to me?”
Jesus answered him, “Allow it for now, for this is how we should fulfill all righteousness.”
Then he allowed him. After being baptized, Jesus immediately came up out of the water. And behold, the heavens opened, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and coming upon him.
And behold, a voice from heaven said, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.”
At that time Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.
After fasting for forty days and forty nights, he was hungry.
The tempter approached and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, command these stones to become bread.”
But he answered, “It is written: A person shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God.” Then the devil took him
into the holy city and set him on the temple gate.

And he said to him, “If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down, for it is written: He will command his angels concerning you, and they will lift you up in their hands, so that you do not strike your foot against a stone.”
Jesus said to him, “It is also written: You shall not put the Lord your God to the test.”
Again the devil took him to a very high mountain and showed him the kingdoms of the world and their glory.
And he said to him, “I will give you all these things if you fall down and worship me.”
Then Jesus said to him, “Get behind me, Satan! For it is written: You shall worship the Lord your God and serve him alone.”
Then the devil left him, and behold, angels came to him and served him.
At that time, when Jesus heard that John had been handed over, he withdrew to Galilee.
Leaving Nazareth, he came and settled in Capernaum by the sea, in the territory of Zebulun.
This was to fulfill what was spoken by the prophet Isaiah, who said:
“Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the way to the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations:
the people sitting in darkness saw a great light, and on those sitting in the land and shadow of death a light has shone.”
From then on, Jesus began to preach and say, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.”
At that time, as Jesus was walking beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon called Peter and Andrew his brother, casting nets into the sea, for they were fishermen.
He said to them, “Follow me, and I will make you fishers of people.”
They left their nets and followed him.
Going on from there, he saw two other brothers, James the son of Zebedee and John his brother, in a boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets. He called them.
They left the boat and their father and followed him.
Jesus went throughout Galilee, teaching in the synagogues, proclaiming the good news of the kingdom, and healing every disease and every illness among the people.
At that time, large crowds followed Jesus from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and the other side of the Jordan.
Seeing the crowd, he went up the mountain, and when he sat down, his disciples came to him.
He opened his mouth and taught them, saying:
“Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.
Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth.
Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be satisfied.
Blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown mercy.
Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.
Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.
Blessed are those persecuted for righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
Blessed are you when people insult you, persecute you, and falsely say every kind of evil against you because of me.
Rejoice and be glad, for your reward in heaven is great.”
The Lord said, “Give to the one who asks you, and do not turn away anyone who wants to borrow from you.
You have heard that it was said, ‘Love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’
But I tell you: Love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat you,
so that you may be children of your heavenly Father. For he makes his sun shine on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the righteous and the unjust.
For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Tax collectors do the same.”
And if you greet your friends, what more are you doing? Do not the tax collectors do the same?
Therefore be perfect, just as your heavenly Father is perfect.
The Lord said: Be careful about your charitable giving. Do not do it before people, so that you will not be seen by them. Otherwise you have no reward from your Father who is in heaven.

So when you give to the poor, do not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, so that people will praise them. Truly I tell you, they will receive their reward.
But when you give to the poor, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing.
Let your charitable giving be in secret, and your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.

And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites, for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues, in the streets, and at crossroads, so that people will see them. Truly I tell you, they will receive their reward.
But when you pray, go into your room, shut your door, and pray to your Father in secret. Your Father sees you in secret and will reward you openly.
When you pray, do not speak needlessly, as the pagans do, for they think they will be heard because of their many words.
Therefore do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask.
Therefore pray like this: Our Father who is in heaven, may your name be held holy.
May your kingdom come. May your will be done on earth as in heaven.
Give us today our bread for the coming day. And
forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors.
And do not lead us into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. For yours is the kingdom and the power and the glory forever. Amen.
The Lord said: If you forgive people their sins, the heavenly Father will forgive you.
But if you do not forgive people their sins, neither will your Father forgive your sins.
When you fast, do not look sad like the hypocrites, for they disfigure their faces so that people will see that they are fasting. Truly I tell you, they will receive their reward.
But when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face.
So that people will not see that you are fasting, but only your Father who is in secret. And your [?] sees in secret and will reward you openly.
Do not store up treasures for yourselves on earth, where worms and decay destroy, and where thieves break in and steal.
Instead, store up treasures for yourselves in heaven, where neither worms nor decay destroy, and where thieves do not break in or steal.
For where your treasure is, there your heart is also.
The Lord said: The eye is the lamp of the body. So if your eye is sound, your whole body is sound.
But if your eye is evil, your whole body is dark. So if the light within you is darkness, how great is that darkness!
For no servant can serve two masters. Either he will hate one and love the other, or he will please one and begin to neglect the other. For he cannot serve God and mammon.
Therefore I tell you: do not worry about your life, what you will eat or what you will drink, or about your body, what you will wear.
Look at the birds of the sky: they neither sow anything nor reap nor gather into barns, yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not worth more than they are?
Which of you, by worrying, can add a single cubit to his height?
And why do you worry about clothing? Let us consider the flowers of the field, how they grow: they neither toil nor spin.
Yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was dressed like one of these.
But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and is thrown into the oven tomorrow, will he not much more clothe you, you of little faith?
Do not worry, saying, ‘What will we eat?’ or ‘What will we drink?’ or ‘What will we wear?’
For the pagans seek all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them all.
But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all this will be given to you. Of God.
So do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Each day has enough trouble of its own.
The Lord said: Do not judge, so that you will not be judged.
For you will be judged with the judgment you use, and you will be measured with the measure you use.
Why do you see the speck in your brother’s eye but do not see the beam in your own eye?
Or how will you say to your brother, ‘Let me remove the speck from your eye’?
Hypocrite, first remove the beam from your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.
Do not give what is holy to dogs, and do not put your pearls before pigs, lest they trample them with their feet and turn around and trample you.
Ask, and it will be given to you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks receives, and whoever seeks finds, and to whoever knocks it will be opened.
The Lord said: Everyone who hears my words and does them, I will compare to a wise man who built his house on rock.
The rain fell, the rivers rose, and the winds blew and beat against that house, but it did not fall, because it had been founded on rock.
And everyone who hears these words of mine and does not do them will be like a foolish man who built his house on sand.
The rain fell, the rivers rose, and the winds blew and beat against that house, and it fell, and its destruction was very great.
And when Jesus had finished all these words, the crowds were amazed at his teaching.
For he taught them as someone who had authority, and not like a scribe and a Pharisee.
When he came down from the mountain, large crowds followed him.
And behold, a leper bowed before him, saying, “Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean.”
Jesus stretched out his hand and touched him, saying, “I am willing to make you clean.” And immediately his leprosy was cleared away.
Jesus said to him, “See that you tell no one, but go, show yourself to the priests, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, as a testimony.”
At that time, when Jesus entered Capernaum, a centurion fell before him, pleading with him and saying,
“Lord, my servant is lying at home, paralyzed and suffering terribly.”
Jesus said to him, “I will come and heal him.”
The centurion answered him, “Lord, I am not worthy for you to come under my roof. But just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
For I too am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I say to this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes, and to another, ‘Come,’ and he comes, and to my slave, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”
When Jesus heard this, he marveled at him and said to those following him, “Truly I tell you, I have not found such great faith even in Israel.
And I tell you that many will come from east and west and recline at table with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.
But the children of the kingdom will be driven out into the outer darkness. There is weeping and gnashing of teeth there.”
And Jesus said to the centurion, “Go; let it be done for you as you have believed.” And his servant was healed at that hour.
At that time, Jesus came into Peter’s house and saw his mother-in-law lying sick with a fever.
He touched her hand, and the fever left her. She got up and served him.
When evening came, they brought him many who were possessed by demons. He drove out the spirits with a word and healed all who were sick.
This was to fulfill what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, who said, “He took our infirmities and bore our illnesses.”
When Jesus saw a large crowd around him, he gave orders to cross over to this side.
A scribe approached and said to him, “Teacher, shall I follow you wherever you go?”
Jesus said to him, “Foxes have dens, and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”
Another of the disciples said to him, “Lord, allow me first to go and bury my father.”
But Jesus said to him, “Follow me, and leave the dead to bury their own dead.”
When he got into the boat, his disciples followed him.
At that time, Jesus came into the land of the Gergesenes. Two demon-possessed men met him, coming out of the tomb. They were so extremely fierce that no one could pass along that road.
And immediately they cried out, saying, “What have we to do with you, Son of God? Have you come before the appointed time to torment us?”
Now a large herd of pigs was feeding a long way from the two of them.
The demons begged him, saying, “If you drive us out, command us to go into the herd of pigs.”
He said to them, “Go.” They went into the pigs, and immediately the whole herd rushed down the bank into the sea and drowned in the water.
The herdsmen fled, went into the town, and reported everything concerning the two demon-possessed men.
Immediately the whole town came out to meet Jesus. When they saw him, they begged him to leave their region. Jesus got into the boat and crossed over to his own town.
Jesus got into the boat and crossed over to his own town.
Immediately they brought him a paralyzed man lying on a bed. When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralyzed man, “Take courage, child. Your sins will be forgiven.”
Immediately some of the scribes said to themselves, “This man is blaspheming.”
Jesus saw their thoughts and said to them, “Why do you think evil things in your hearts?”
“For which is easier: to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk’?”
“But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the paralyzed man, “Get up, take your bed, and go to your home.”
When the crowds saw this, they were amazed and glorified God, who had given such authority to human beings.
At that time, as Jesus passed by, he saw a man named Matthew sitting at the tax booth. He said to him, “Follow me.” He got up and followed him.
While he was reclining at a meal in the house, many sinners and tax collectors came and reclined with Jesus and his disciples.
When the Pharisees saw this, they said to his disciples, “Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?”
Jesus said to them, “Healthy people do not need a doctor, but sick people do.”
“Go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice.’ For I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
At that time, a ruler fell down before Jesus and bowed to him, saying, “My daughter is about to die now. But come and lay your hand on her, and she will live.”
Jesus got up and followed him, along with his disciples. She approached from behind and touched the edge of his garment.
And there was a woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years.
She said, “If I only touch the edge of his garment, I will be healed.”
Jesus turned around and said, “Take courage, daughter. Your faith will heal you.” And the woman was healed from that hour.
Jesus came into the ruler’s house and saw her sleeping and the crowd making a commotion. He said to them:
“Go away, for the girl will not die, but is sleeping.” And they laughed at him.
When he had driven out the whole crowd, he went in and took her by the hand, and the girl got up.
And this news spread throughout that whole land.
At that time, Jesus passed by, and two blind men followed him, crying out and saying, “Have mercy on us, Son of David!”
When he entered the house, the blind men fell down before him, and Jesus said to them, “Do you believe that I can do this?” They said, “Yes, Lord.”
Then he touched their eyes, saying, “Let it be done for you according to your faith.”
And their eyes were opened. And he sternly warned them, saying, “See that you tell no one.”
But they went away and spread his fame throughout that whole land.
As they were leaving, people immediately brought him a deaf man possessed by a demon.
And when the demon had been driven out, the deaf man spoke. The crowds marveled, saying, “Nothing like this has ever appeared in Jerusalem.”
But the Pharisees said, “He drives out demons by the ruler of demons.”
And Jesus went through all the towns and all the [?], teaching in the synagogues, proclaiming the good news of the kingdom, and healing every sickness and every affliction among the people.
Jesus called his twelve disciples and gave them authority over unclean spirits, to drive them out and to heal every sickness and every disease.
He sent these twelve out, commanding them and saying, “Go on the road to the Gentiles, and do not enter a Samaritan town.”
“But go instead to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”
“As you go, proclaim, saying, ‘The kingdom of heaven has drawn near.’”
“Heal the sick; raise the dead. You received freely; give freely as well.”
“Everyone who acknowledges me before others, I too will acknowledge before the heavenly Father.”
“But whoever denies me before others, I too will deny before the heavenly Father.”
“Whoever loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me, and whoever loves son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.”
“Whoever does not take up his cross and follows me is not worthy of me.”
“Whoever finds his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for my sake will find it.”
“Whoever welcomes you welcomes me.”
“Whoever welcomes a prophet because he is a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward, and whoever welcomes a righteous person because he is righteous will receive a righteous person’s reward.”
“And whoever gives one of these little ones even a cup of cold water to drink because he is a disciple—truly I tell you, he will not lose his reward.”
“To you, and more than a prophet.”
“For this is the one about whom it is written: ‘See, I will send a messenger ahead of you, who will prepare your way before you.’”
Truly I tell you, among those born of women no one greater than John the Baptist has arisen. Yet the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.
From the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven suffers violence, and violent people seize it.
For all the prophets and the Law prophesied until John.
And if you are willing to accept it, he is Elijah who is to come.
Let anyone who has ears to hear listen.
Everything has been handed over to me by my Father. No one knows the Son except the Father, nor does anyone know the Father except the Son and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal him.
Come to me, all who toil and are burdened, and I will give you rest.
Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
Many crowds came, and he healed them all.
And he warned them not to make him known.
This was to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah, who said:
Here is my servant whom I have chosen, my beloved, in whom my soul delights. I will put my Spirit upon him, and he will proclaim justice to the nations.
He will not quarrel or cry out, nor will anyone hear his voice at the crossroads.
He will not break a bruised reed, and he will not extinguish a burning [?], until he brings justice to victory.
And the nations will hope in his name.
The Lord said: Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.
Therefore I tell you, every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven people, but blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven people.
Whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, either in this age or in the age to come.
Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree rotten and its fruit rotten, for a tree is known by its fruit.
You brood of vipers! How can you speak good things when you are evil? For the mouth speaks from the abundance of the heart.
A good person brings good things out of a good vessel, and an evil person brings evil things out of an evil vessel.
But I tell you that people will give an account on the day of judgment for every idle word they speak.
For by your own words you will be justified.
The kingdom of heaven is like a merchant seeking fine pearls.
who, on finding a very valuable pearl, went and sold all his possessions, everything he had, and bought it.
Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a net thrown into the sea that gathered creatures of every kind.
When it was full, they pulled it ashore, sat down, and sorted the good ones into containers, but threw the bad ones away.
So it will be at the end of the age. The angels will come out and separate the wicked from among the righteous,
and throw them into the fiery furnace. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
Jesus said, “Do you understand all these things?” They said to him, “Yes, Lord.”
Then Jesus said to them, “Therefore every scribe who has been instructed in the kingdom of heaven is like a householder who brings out of his storeroom things both new and old.”
And when Jesus had finished this parable, he departed from there.
He came to his hometown and taught them in their synagogues.
At that time, Jesus saw a large crowd, had compassion on them, and healed their sick.

When it grew late, his disciples approached him, saying, “This is a deserted place, and the hour is already past. Send the crowds away so that they may go into the surrounding villages and buy themselves food.”
But Jesus said to them, “You give them something to eat.”
They said, “We have nothing here except five loaves and two fish.”
He said, “Bring them here.”

He told the crowd to recline on the grass. Taking the five loaves and both fish, he looked up to heaven and blessed them. He broke the loaves and gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the crowds.
They all ate and were satisfied, and they gathered up the leftover pieces, twelve full baskets.
Those who ate numbered five thousand men, besides women and children.
Immediately he urged the disciples to get into the boat and go ahead to the other side while he dismissed the crowds.
After dismissing the crowd, he went up the mountain alone to pray.
When it was late, at the fourth hour of the night, Jesus came to them, walking on the sea.
When his disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were afraid, saying, “It is a ghost!” And they cried out in fear.
Jesus said to them, “Take courage, for it is I. Do not be afraid.”
Peter answered him, “Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you.”
Jesus said to him, “Come.” Peter got out of the boat, walked on the water, and came to Jesus.
But when he saw the fierce wind, he became afraid. Beginning to sink, he cried out, “Lord, save me!”
Jesus stretched out his hand, caught him, and said to him, “You of little faith, why did you doubt?”
When he got into the boat, the wind died down.
Those in the boat bowed down before him, saying, “Truly you are the Son of God.”
After crossing over, they came to the land of Gennesaret.
At that time, Jesus entered the region of Tyre and Sidon.
And a Canaanite woman from that region came out and cried, “Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David! My daughter is badly tormented by a demon.”
But he did not answer her a word. His disciples came up and begged him, saying, “Send her away, for she keeps crying out after us.”
He answered, “I was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”
But she came and bowed down before him, saying, “Lord, help me.”
He answered, “It is not right to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs.”
She said, “Yes, Lord, but even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their masters’ table.”
Then Jesus answered her, “Woman, great is your faith! Let it be done for you as you wish.” And her daughter was healed at that very hour.

At that time, Jesus called his disciples and said to them, “I feel compassion for the crowd, because they have stayed with me for three days now and have nothing to eat. I do not want to send them away without eating, lest they faint on the way.”
His disciples said to him, “Where can we get enough bread in this deserted place to feed such a large crowd?”
Jesus said to them, “How many loaves do you have?” They said, “Seven, and a few small fish.”
Jesus told the crowd to sit down on the ground.
Jesus took the bread and fish, offered praise, broke them, and gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the crowd.
They all ate and were satisfied, and they gathered seven full baskets of leftover pieces.
Those who ate numbered four thousand, besides women and children.
After sending the crowd away, he got into the boat and crossed over to the region of Magdala.
At that time, a man approached Jesus and bowed down
before him, saying, “Lord, have mercy on my son, for he is afflicted by a demon at the new moon and suffers terribly. He often falls into the fire and often into the water.
I brought him to your disciples, but they could not heal him.”
Jesus answered, “Faithless and corrupt generation! How long will I be with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring him here to me.”
Jesus rebuked him, and immediately the demon came out of him, and the boy was healed from that hour.
And the disciples approached Jesus when he was alone and said, “Why could we not drive it out?”

Jesus said to them, “Because of your unbelief. Truly I tell you, if you have faith like a mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move. And nothing will be impossible for you.”
“But this kind comes out by nothing except prayer and fasting.”
While they were staying in Galilee, Jesus said, “The Son of Man is going to be handed over into the hands of sinners.”
“And they will kill him, and on the third day he will rise.”
At that time, those who collected the two-drachma tax approached Peter and said to him, “Does your teacher not pay the two-drachma tax?”

Peter said to them, “Yes.” And when they went into the house, Jesus spoke to Peter first, saying, “What do you think, Simon? From whom do earthly kings collect taxes or tribute—from their own sons or from strangers?”
Peter said to him, “From strangers.” And Jesus said to him:

“But so that we do not cause them to stumble, go to the sea and cast a hook. Take the first fish that is caught and open its mouth. You will find a stater. Take it and give it to them for me and for yourself.”
And immediately, at that hour, his disciples fell down before him, saying, “Who, then, is greatest in the kingdom of heaven?”
And Jesus called a child and placed the child among them.

And he said, “Truly, truly I tell you, unless you turn and become like children, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven. Whoever humbles himself like this child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.”
The Lord said, “Take care not to neglect one of these little ones, for I tell you that their angels in heaven always see the face of my heavenly Father.”

“For the Son of Man came to seek and save the lost. What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them goes missing, will he not leave the ninety-nine on the mountains and go and look for the lost one?”
“And if he finds it, truly I tell you, he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine that did not go missing.”
“In the same way, it is not the will of your heavenly Father that one of these little ones should perish.”
“If your brother sins against you, go and confront him, just between you and him alone. If he listens to you, you will have won back your brother.”
“But if he does not listen to you, take one or two others with you, so that every matter may be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.”
“If he refuses to listen to them, tell the church. And if he disregards even the church, let him be to you like a pagan and a tax collector.”
“Truly I tell you, whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you release on earth will be released in heaven.”
“Again, truly I tell you that if two of you agree on earth about anything you ask, it will be done for them by my heavenly Father.”
“For where two or three are gathered in my name, I am there among them.”
The Lord told this parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like a king who decided to settle accounts with his servants.”
“When he began to settle accounts, a man who owed ten thousand talents was brought to him.”
“And since he had nothing with which to repay, his master ordered that he be sold, along with his wife and all his possessions.”
Then that servant fell down and bowed before him, saying, “Master, be patient with me, and I will repay you everything.”
The master of that servant had compassion on him, released him, and canceled his debt.
But that servant went out and found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred [?] coins. He seized him and beat him, saying, “Pay me what you owe.”
Then that fellow servant fell down and begged him, saying, “Be patient with me, and I will repay you.”
But he refused. Instead, he took him away and put him in prison until he should repay his whole debt.
When his fellow servants saw what was happening, they were deeply distressed. They went and told his master everything that had happened.
Then his master summoned him and said to him, “You wicked servant! I forgave you your whole debt because you begged me.
Should you not also have had mercy on your fellow servant, just as I had mercy on you?”
His master became angry and handed him over to the torturers until he should repay his whole debt.
So also my heavenly Father will do to you, unless each of you forgives his brother’s sins from your hearts. Amen.
At that time the Pharisees seized Jesus, testing him and saying, “Is it lawful to divorce this woman for any reason?”
He answered them, “Have you not read that he created them in the beginning, making them male and female,
and said, ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to her, and the two will become one flesh’?
Therefore, what God has joined together, let no one separate—this woman [?].”
The Pharisees said to him, “Why then did Moses command that a certificate of divorce be given and the woman be divorced?”
Jesus said to them, “Because of your hardness of heart, he allowed you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it was not so.
But I tell you: whoever divorces his wife when she has not committed adultery, and makes her commit adultery, commits adultery.”
His disciples said to him, “If this is the situation of a man with his wife, it is better not to marry.”
Jesus said to them, “Not all of you understand this saying, but only those to whom it has been given.

For there are eunuchs who were so from their mother’s womb, and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by other people, and there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. Let those who can accept this accept it.”
At that time a certain young man came to Jesus, saying, “Good teacher, what good thing must I do to receive eternal life?”
He said to him, “Why do you call me good? For no one is good except God alone. But if you wish to enter life, keep the commandments.”
The young man said to him, “Which ones?” Jesus said to him, “Do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal, and do not listen to falsehood.
Honor your father and mother, and love your neighbor as yourself.” The young man said to him,
“I have kept all these things from my youth. What do I still lack?”
Jesus said to him, “Do you wish to be perfect? Go, sell all your possessions and give to the poor, and you will receive the kingdom of heaven. Then come, follow me.”
When the young man heard this, he went away sorrowful, for he had great wealth.
Jesus said to his disciples, “Truly, truly, I tell you, it is not easy for a rich person to enter the kingdom of heaven.”
“For it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.”
When his disciples heard this, they were astonished and said, “Who can be saved?”
Jesus looked at them and said, “For human beings this is impossible, but for God these things are possible.”
Peter answered him, “Lord, look, we have left everything and followed you. What, then, will we have?”

Jesus said to them, “Truly, truly, I tell you, you who have followed me will be again [?]. When the Son of Man sits on the throne of his glory, you too will sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”
“And everyone who has left brothers or sisters, father or mother, wife or children, fields or houses for my name’s sake will receive a hundredfold reward and inherit eternal life.”
“But the first will be last, and the last will be first.”
“The kingdom of heaven is like a landowner who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.”
“After agreeing on a wage of one silver coin each, he sent them into the vineyard. Going out at the third hour, he saw others standing idle in the marketplace.”
“He said to them, ‘You too go into my vineyard, and I will give you whatever is fair.’”
“So they went. He went out again at the sixth and tenth hours and did the same.”
“Going out at the eleventh hour, he found others standing idle and said to them, ‘Why have you been standing here idle all day?’”
“They said to him, ‘Because no one has hired us.’ He said to them, ‘You too go into my vineyard, and you will receive whatever the wage is.’”
“When evening came, the master said to the vineyard manager, ‘Call the workers and give them their wages, beginning with the last and continuing to the first.’”
“Those who had come at the eleventh hour each received one coin.”
“Those who had come first thought they would receive more [?].”
At that time, Jesus was leaving Jericho, and a large crowd was following him.
And there were two blind men sitting beside the road. When they heard that Jesus was passing by, they cried out, “Have mercy on us, Lord, Son of David!”
The crowds rebuked them, telling them to be quiet, but they cried out all the more, “Have mercy on us, Lord, Son of David!”
Jesus stopped, called them, and said, “What do you want me to do for you?”
They said to him, “Lord, let our eyes be opened.”
Moved with compassion, Jesus touched their eyes. Immediately the eyes of both men were opened, and they followed him.
At that time, when Jesus drew near to Jerusalem and came to Bethphage, to the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples
and said to them, “Go into the village opposite you, and immediately you will find a donkey tied up, with a colt beside it. Untie them and bring them here.
And if anyone says anything to you, say, ‘The Lord needs [?] them,’ and he sent them.”
All this happened so that what was spoken by the prophet might be fulfilled:
“Say to the daughter of Zion, ‘Look, your king is coming to you, gentle and riding on a donkey and a colt, the offspring of a beast of burden.’”
The disciples went and did as Jesus had commanded them.
They brought the donkey and the colt and laid their cloaks on them, and he sat on them.
Great crowds spread their cloaks on the road, while others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.
The crowds going ahead of him and following behind cried out, “Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!”
When he entered Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred up, and they said, “Who is this?”
The crowds said, “This is Jesus the prophet, from Nazareth in Galilee.”
When the chief priests and scribes saw the wonders he was doing and the children crying out in the temple, “Hosanna to the Son of David!” they were indignant
and said to him, “Do you hear what these children are saying?” Jesus said to them, “Yes. Have you not read, ‘From the mouths of infants and nursing babies you have perfected praise’?”
He left them and went out of the city to Bethany, and stayed there.
The Lord told this parable: “There was a rich man who planted a vineyard, dug a winepress in it, leased it to tenants, and went away.
When the time came to collect it, he sent his servants to the tenants to collect his wine.
The tenants seized his servants, beat some, killed others, and stoned still others.
Again he sent other servants, more than the first, and they treated them in the same way.
Last of all, he sent his son to them, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’
But when the tenants saw his son, they said to one another, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him and take possession of his inheritance.’
They seized him, took him out of the vineyard, and killed him.
So when the owner of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those tenants?” They said to him,
“He will bring those wicked men to a terrible end and lease the vineyard to other tenants, who will give him the fruit at the proper times.”
Jesus said to them, “Have you not read in the Scriptures, ‘The stone they rejected has become the cornerstone. This came from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes’?”
At that time, the Pharisees plotted against Jesus to trap him in his words.

And they sent their disciples to him with the Herodians, saying, “Teacher, we know that you are truthful and teach the way of God in truth. You are not concerned about anyone, for you do not judge people by their standing.
Tell us, then, what you think: is it lawful for us to pay tax to Caesar or not?”
But Jesus, knowing their malice, said to them, “Why are you testing me, you hypocrites?
Show me the coin used for the tax.” And they brought him a denarius.
And Jesus said to them, “What is this image [?] and inscription?”
They said to him, “Caesar’s.” Jesus said to them, “Then give back to Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and to God what belongs to God.”
When they heard this, they marveled, and they left him and went away.
At that time, an expert in the law came to Jesus, testing him, and bowed before him, saying,
“Teacher, which commandment is greatest in the law?”
Jesus said to him, “Love the Lord your God with all your heart.
This is the great commandment.
And here is a second like it: love your neighbor as yourself.
On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.”
While the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus questioned them,
saying, “What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is he?” They said to him, “David’s.”
Jesus said to them, “How, then, does David, speaking by the Spirit, call him Lord, saying,
‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet”’?
If, then, he calls him Lord by the Spirit, how is he his son?”
And no one could answer him a word, nor did anyone dare from that day on to question him any further.
At that time, as Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives, his disciples came to him, saying, “Tell us, when will this happen, and what will be the sign of your coming and of the end of the age?”
Jesus answered and said to them, “Take care that no one deceives you.
For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am the Christ,’ and they will deceive many.
You will hear of wars and reports of wars. See that you are not alarmed, for all these things must happen, but the end will not come then.
For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be famines and plagues and earthquakes in various places.
All these things are the beginning of birth pains.
Then they will hand you over to suffering and kill you, and you will be hated by all nations because of my name.
Then many will fall away, betray one another, and hate one another.
Many false prophets will arise and lead many astray.
Because lawlessness increases, the love of many will grow cold.
But whoever endures to the end will be saved.
This good news of the kingdom will be proclaimed throughout the whole world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come.
So when you see the abomination of desolation spoken of by the prophet Daniel standing in the holy place—let the reader understand—
then those who are in Judea must flee to the mountains.
Whoever is on the rooftop must not go down [?] what is in his house.
Likewise, whoever is in the field must not turn back to get his clothes.
But woe to pregnant women and nursing mothers on that day!
Pray that your flight will not be in winter or on the Sabbath.
For then there will be great suffering, such as has not occurred from the beginning of the world until now, but will occur.
If those days had not been shortened, no one would be saved. But for the sake of the chosen, those days will be shortened.
Then if anyone says to you, ‘Look, the Christ is here,’ do not believe it.
For false Christs and false prophets will arise and perform great signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen.
Look, I have told you beforehand.
If they say to you, ‘Look, he is in the wilderness,’ do not go out. ‘Look, he is in the inner rooms,’ do not believe it.
For just as lightning comes from the east and is visible as far as the west, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.
For wherever the corpse is, there the eagles will gather.
Immediately after the suffering of those days, the sun will grow dark, the moon will not give its light, the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of heaven will be shaken.
Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn. They will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
He will send angels with a loud trumpet blast, and they will gather his chosen from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other.
Learn the lesson of the fig tree: when its branch becomes tender and its leaves sprout, you know that the harvest is near.
Likewise, when you see all these things, see that he is near, at the doors.
Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things happen.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
But no one knows about that day and hour, not even the angels of heaven, only the Father alone.
As in the days of Noah, so will be the coming of the Son [?] a paralyzed man, and they were trying to bring him in and lay him before him.
For in the days before the flood, they were eating and drinking, marrying and being given in marriage, until the day Noah entered the ark.
And they did not realize it until the flood came and swept them all away. So will be the coming of the Son of Man.
Then two men will be in the field; one will be taken and the other left.
Two women will be grinding at the mill; one will be taken and the other left.
So stay awake, because you do not know at what hour your Lord will come.
But know this: if the master of the house had known during which watch of the night the thief would come, he would have stayed awake and would not have allowed his house to be broken into.
Therefore you too must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour when you do not expect him.
Who, then, is the faithful and wise servant whom the master will put in charge of his household, to give them their food at the proper time?
Blessed is that servant whom his master finds doing this when he comes.
Truly, truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of his whole household.
But if that wicked servant says in his heart, ‘My master is taking a long time to come,’
and begins to beat his fellow servants and to eat and drink with drunkards,
that servant’s master will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he does not know.
He will cut him in two and assign him a place with the hypocrites. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
Then the kingdom of heaven was compared to ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom and the bride.
Five of them were foolish and five were wise.
For the foolish ones took their lamps but did not take any oil with them.
But the wise ones took oil in containers along with their lamps.
As the bridegroom was delayed, they all grew drowsy and slept.
But at midnight there was a shout: ‘Look, the bridegroom is coming! Go out to meet him!’
Then all those virgins got up and put their lamps in order.
And the foolish said to the wise, “Give us some of your oil, because our lamps are going out.”
The wise answered, saying, “There may not be enough for both us and you. Go instead to those who sell it.”
To buy. The bridegroom came, and those who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast, and the doors were shut.
Afterward the other virgins also came, saying, “Lord, Lord, open the door for us.”
But he answered, “Truly, truly, I tell you, I do not know you.”
Therefore keep watch, because you do not know the day or the hour when the Son of Man will come.
For it is like a man going away, who called his servants and handed over his property.
To one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one, to each according to his own ability. And immediately he went away.
The one who had received five talents went and traded with them and gained another five talents.
Likewise, the one who had received two gained another two.
But the one who had received one went and dug in the ground and hid his master’s money.
After a long time, the master of those servants came and settled accounts with them.
The one who had received five talents came forward and said, “Master, you entrusted me with five talents. Look, I have gained another five with them.”
His master said to him, “Well done, good and faithful servant. You were faithful over a little; I will put you in charge of much. Enter into your master’s joy.”
The one who had received two talents came forward and said, “Master, you entrusted me with two talents. Look, I have gained another two with them.”
His master said to him, “Well done, good and faithful servant. You were faithful over a little; I will put you in charge of much. Enter into your master’s joy.”
The one who had received one talent also came forward and said, “Master, I knew that you are a harsh man, reaping where you have not sown and gathering where you have not scattered.
So I was afraid and went and hid your talent in the ground. Look, you have what is yours.”
His master answered him, “You wicked and lazy servant. You knew that I reap where I have not sown and gather where I have not scattered.
You should therefore have deposited my money with the bankers, and when I came, I would have received it back with interest.
So take the talent from him and give it to the one who has ten talents.
For the one who has will be given everything and will have an abundance. But from the one who does not have, even what he thinks he has will be taken away. And
throw the useless servant into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth there.”
When the Son of Man comes in his glory:

And all the nations will be gathered before him, and he will separate them from one another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats. And he will place the sheep on his right and the goats on his left.
Then the Father will say to those on his right, “Come, you who are blessed by my Father. Inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the whole world.”
“For I was hungry, and you gave me food. I was thirsty, and you gave me a drink. I was a stranger, and you took me in.”
“I was naked, and you clothed me. I was sick, and you visited me. I was in prison, and you came to me.”
Then the righteous will answer him, saying, “Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you a drink?”
“And when did we see you as a stranger and take you in, or naked and clothe you?”
“And when did we see you sick or in prison and come to you?”
And the King will answer them, “Truly, truly I tell you, since you did it for one of these little ones, the least of my brothers, you did it for me.”
Then he will also say to those on his left, “Depart from me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.”
“For I was hungry, and you gave me no food. I was thirsty, and you gave me no drink.”
“I was a stranger, and you did not take me in. I was sick and in prison, and you did not visit me.”
Then they too will answer, saying, “Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison and not visit you?”
Then he will answer them, saying, “Truly, truly I tell you, since you did not do it for one of these least ones, neither did you do it for me.”
And they will go into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.
“You know that in two days the Passover will come, and the Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified.”
Then the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders of the people gathered in the courtyard of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas.
And they plotted to seize Jesus by deceit and kill him.
But they said, “Not during the festival, so that there will not be an uproar among the people.”
Now when Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,
a woman came to him with an alabaster jar of expensive perfume and poured it on his head as he reclined at the table.
When his disciples saw this, they were indignant and said, “Why this waste?”
“For this perfume could have been sold for a large sum and the money given to the poor.”
But Jesus knew this and said to them, “Why are you troubling the woman? She has done a good deed for me.”
“For you always have the poor with you, but you do not always have me.”
“By pouring this perfume on my body, she has prepared me for burial.”
“Truly I tell you, wherever this gospel is preached in the whole world, what she does will also be spoken of in her memory.” Gospel 3.
Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
and said, “What will you give me if I hand him over to you?” They agreed to give him thirty silver coins.
From then on he looked for a suitable opportunity to hand him over.
On the first day of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came to Jesus and said to him, “Where do you want us to prepare for you to eat the Passover meal?”
He said, “Go into the city to a certain man and tell him, ‘The Teacher says: My time is near. I will celebrate the Passover at your house with my disciples.’”
The disciples did as Jesus had instructed them and prepared the Passover meal.
When evening came, he reclined at the table with the twelve disciples.
While they were eating, he said, “Truly I tell you, one of you will betray me.”
They were deeply distressed, and each of them began to say to him, “Is it I, Lord?”
He answered, “The one who dipped his hand with me will betray me.”
“The Son of Man goes as it is written about him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would have been better for that man if he had not been born.”
Judas, who was betraying him, answered, “Is it I, Teacher?” He said to him, “You have said it.”
While they were eating, Jesus took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to his disciples, saying, “Take and eat; this is my body.”
Then he took a cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, “Drink from it, all of you.”
“This is my blood of the new covenant, poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.”
“But I tell you, I will no longer drink from this fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father’s kingdom.”
After singing praises, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Then Jesus said to them, “You will all fall away because of me this night, for it is written: ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will scatter.’”
“But after my resurrection, I will go ahead of you to Galilee.”
Peter answered him, “Even if everyone falls away because of you, I will never fall away.”
Jesus said to him, “Truly I tell you, this very night, before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.”
Peter said to him, “Even if I must die with you, I will not deny you.” All the disciples said the same.
Then Jesus came with them to a village called Gethsemane and said to the disciples, “Sit here while I go over there and pray.”
He took Peter and the two sons of Zebedee with him and began to be distressed and troubled.
Then Jesus said, “My soul is sorrowful to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch with me.”
And going a little farther, he fell face down, praying and saying, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me. Yet not as I will, but as you will.”
He came to the disciples and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, “Could you not keep watch with me for one hour?
Keep watch and pray, so that you do not enter into temptation. For the spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
Again he went away a second time and prayed, saying, “Father, if this cup cannot pass from me unless I drink it, your will be done.”
When he came back, he again found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy.
And leaving them, he went away again and prayed a third time, saying the same words.
Then he came to the disciples and said to them, “Sleep on now and rest. Look, the hour has drawn near, and the Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of sinners.
Get up, let us go. Look, the one who betrays me has drawn near.”
And while he was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, arrived, and with him a large crowd with swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests and the elders of the people.
Now his betrayer had given them a sign, saying, “The one I kiss is the man. Seize him.”
And immediately he approached Jesus and said to him, “Greetings, Teacher!” And he kissed him.
But Jesus said to him, “Friend, do what you have come for.” Then they came forward, laid hands on Jesus, and seized him.
And look, one of those who were with Jesus struck the high priest’s servant and cut off his ear.
Then Jesus said to him, “Put your sword back in its place, for all who take up the sword will perish by the sword.
Or do you think that I cannot now appeal to my Father, and he will provide me with more than twelve legions of angels?
How, then, would the Scriptures be fulfilled, which say that it must happen this way?”
At that time Jesus said to the crowds, “Have you come out with swords and clubs to seize me as though I were a robber? Every day I sat with you in the temple, teaching, and you did not seize me.
But all this happened so that the writings of the prophets might be fulfilled.” Then all the disciples abandoned him and fled.
Those who had seized Jesus led him to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders had gathered.
But Peter followed him at a distance, as far as the high priest’s courtyard. He went into the courtyard and sat with the servants, wanting to see the outcome.
Now the chief priests and the elders and the whole council were seeking false witnesses against Jesus so that they could put him to death,
but they found none. And though many witnesses came forward, they found none. Finally, two false witnesses came forward and said,
“This man said, ‘I can destroy the temple of God and rebuild it in three days.’”
And the high priest stood up and said to him, “Have you no answer? What are these men testifying?”
But Jesus remained silent. And the high priest spoke to him, saying, “I put you under oath by the living God: tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God.”
Jesus said to him, “You have said so. But I tell you, from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the Father and coming on the clouds of heaven.”
Then the high priest tore his clothes, saying, “He has spoken blasphemy! What further need do we have of witnesses? Look, you have now heard his blasphemy.”
“What do you think?” They answered, “He deserves death.”
Then they spat in his face and mistreated him, and others struck him on the cheek,
saying, “Prophesy to us, Christ! Who was it that struck you?”
Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard, and a servant girl came up to him and said, “You too were with Jesus the Galilean.”
But he denied it before everyone, saying, “I do not know what you are talking about.”
When he went out to the gateway, another servant girl saw him and said to those there, “This man too was with Jesus the Nazarene.”
Again he denied it with an oath: “I do not know the man.”
A little later, those standing nearby came up and said to Peter, “You really are one of them, for your speech gives you away.”
Then he began to call down curses on himself and swear, “I do not know this man.” Immediately a rooster crowed.
Peter remembered the words Jesus had spoken to him: “Before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.” He went outside and wept bitterly.
At that time, the chief priests and the elders of the people took counsel against Jesus to put him to death.
They bound him, led him away, and handed him over to Pontius Pilate, the governor.
When Judas, who had betrayed him, saw that he had been condemned, he repented and returned the thirty silver coins to the chief priests and elders,
saying, “I have sinned by betraying innocent blood.” But they said, “What is that to us? See to it yourself.”
He threw the silver into the temple and left. Then he went away and hanged himself.
The chief priests took the silver and said, “It is not lawful to put it into the treasury, since it is the price of blood.”
After taking counsel, they used it to buy the potter’s field as a burial place for strangers.
Therefore that field has been called the Field of Blood to this day.
Then the word spoken by the prophet Isaiah was fulfilled: “And he took the thirty silver coins, the price of the one whose value had been set by the sons of Israel,
and they gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord directed me.”
Jesus stood before the governor, and the governor asked him, “Are you the King of the Jews?” Jesus said to him, “You say so.”
When the chief priests and elders accused him, he made no reply.
Pilate said to him, “Do you not hear how much they are testifying against you?”
And he did not answer them a single word, so that the governor was greatly amazed.
At every festival, the governor was accustomed to release to the crowd a prisoner whom they wanted.
At that time they had a notorious prisoner called Barabbas.
When they had gathered, Pilate said, “Which of the two do you want me to release to you: Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?”
For he knew that they had handed him over out of envy.
While he was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent him a message, saying, “Have nothing to do with that righteous man, for I have suffered greatly today in a dream because of him.”
But the chief priests and the elders persuaded the crowds to ask for Barabbas and to have Jesus put to death.
The governor said to them, “Which of the two do you want me to release to you?” They said, “Barabbas.”
Pilate said to them, “What shall I do with Jesus who is called Christ?” They all said, “Let him be crucified!”
The governor said to them, “What evil has this man done?” But they shouted all the louder, saying, “Let him be crucified!”

When Pilate saw that he was accomplishing nothing, but that an uproar was beginning instead, he took water and washed his hands before the crowd, saying, “I am innocent of this righteous man’s blood. See to it yourselves.”
All the people answered, “His blood be on us and on our children.”
Then he released Barabbas to them, but had Jesus flogged and handed him over to them to be crucified.
Then the governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the governor’s headquarters and gathered the whole cohort around him.
They stripped him and put a scarlet cloak on him.
They wove a crown of thorns and placed it on his head, and put a reed in his right hand. Then they knelt before him and mocked him, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!”
They spat on him, took the reed, and struck him on the head.
When they had mocked him, they took the cloak off him, put his own clothes on him, and led him away to be crucified.
As they went out, they found a man from Cyrene named Simon. They forced him to carry Jesus’ cross.
The soldiers came to a place called Golgotha, which is called the Place of the Skull.
They gave him vinegar mixed with gall to drink, but when he tasted it, he would not drink.
After crucifying him, they divided his clothes and cast lots.
Then they sat down and kept watch over him there.
Above his head they placed the written charge against him: “This is the King of the Jews.”
Then two robbers were crucified with him, one on his right and one on his left.
Those passing by insulted him, shaking their heads.
They said, “Aha! You who destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days, save yourself! If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross.”
Likewise, the chief priests mocked him, and the scribes, elders, and chief priests said:
“He saved others, but he cannot save himself. If he is the King of Israel, let him come down from the cross, and we will believe in him.
He trusted in God; let God rescue him now, if he wants him. For he said that he is the Son of God.”
The two robbers crucified with him also insulted him in the same way.
From the sixth hour, darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.
About the ninth hour, Jesus cried out in a loud voice, saying, “Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani,” which means, “God, my God, why have you abandoned me?”
Some of those standing there heard this and said, “He is calling Elijah.”
Immediately one of them ran, took a sponge full of vinegar, put it on a reed, and gave him a drink.
But the others said, “Leave him alone. Let us see whether Elijah comes to save him.” Another took a spear and pierced his side, and water and blood came out.
Jesus cried out in a loud voice and gave up his spirit.
And behold, the temple curtain was torn in two from top to bottom. The earth shook, and the rocks split apart.
The tombs were opened, and many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep [?] rose.
After his resurrection, they came out of the tomb, entered the holy city, and appeared to many.
When the centurion and those with him who were guarding Jesus saw the earthquake, they were greatly afraid and said, “Truly, he was the Son of God.”
On the Sabbath evening, as the first day of the week was dawning, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.
And behold, there was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord came down from heaven, approached, rolled the stone away from the tomb, and sat on it.
His appearance was like lightning, and his clothing was white as snow.
The guards trembled with fear of him and became like dead men.
The angel said to the women, “Do not be afraid. I know that you are looking for Jesus, who was crucified.
He is not here, for he has risen, just as he said. Come and see the place where the Lord lay.
Go quickly and tell his disciples that he has risen from the dead. And behold, he is going ahead of you to Galilee. You will see him there. See, I have told you.”
They left the tomb quickly, with fear and great joy, and ran to tell his disciples. As they were going to tell his disciples,
Jesus himself met them and said, “Rejoice!” They approached, took hold of his feet, and worshiped him.
Then Jesus said, “Do not be afraid. Go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee. They will see me there.”
While the two women were on their way, some of the guards came into the city and reported to the chief priests
everything that had happened. And the elders gathered together, and after taking counsel, they gave the soldiers a large amount of silver,
saying, “Say, ‘His disciples came at night and stole him while we were sleeping.’
And if the governor hears about this, we will persuade him and keep you out of trouble.”
They took the silver and did as they had been instructed. And this story has spread among the Jews to this day.
The eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had told them to go.
When they saw him, they worshiped him, but some doubted.
Jesus came up and said to them, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me.
Therefore go and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit,
teaching them everything I have commanded you. And look, I am with you every day until the end of the age. Amen.”
